description: Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU), NHERI 2023: Assessing the Effect of 3D Printed Model Quality on Wind Pressure Distribution is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Arindam Gan Chowdhury, Florida International University (fiu.edu). 3D printed models are commonly used in small scale wind tunnel testing. However, print quality can vary depending on 3D printer, nozzle size, and setting chosen. This paper investigates the effect 3D print quality has on the wind pressure distribution of models. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-fqe9-7437. Keywords: NHERI Wall of Wind; wind pressure distribution; structure roughness; 3D printed models. Published 2023-08-22. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
